mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown accelerating week-on-week recovery (-72.6, -67.3, -57.6, -41.1), with the gain size itself growing each week. This momentum in the series' own trajectory should persist, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:weekly increments of 5.3, 9.7, 16.5 points show accelerating recovery
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite the prior accelerating weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: A large cumulative improvement in WORKPLACES mobility over three consecutive weeks indicates commuting and office-linked foot traffic is normalizing, which should pull retail footfall upward within two weeks as workers resume lunch and after-work shopping routines near offices.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by 15 points or more cumulatively over the prior 3 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -64.0 to -40.6, a 23.4 point gain over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the subsequent two weeks even though WORKPLACES met or exceeded the 15-point cumulative threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve sharply in the same week, the combined restoration of commuting infrastructure use and office attendance produces a compounding effect on discretionary retail visits that exceeds the sum of either series improving alone, since workers both travel through and linger near retail hubs.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 15.0 points and WORKPLACES rose 9.4 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the following four weeks is no greater than what is predicted from either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES improving alone, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen steadily from 24.3 to 12.7 percent above baseline, indicating households are spending less time confined at home under a reopening policy regime. As RESIDENTIAL approaches baseline, this released time converts into out-of-home discretionary activity, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 24.3 to 12.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its decline toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If the pace of recovery in GROCERY_PHARM (an essential, policy-sensitive category) decelerates sharply after its rapid gains, this signals an emerging tightening of restrictions or caution from authorities responding to a case resurgence, which would subsequently suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC mobility as similar curbs extend to non-essential categories.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week improvement in GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5 points after two weeks of gains exceeding 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM gained 20.5 points from t-1w to t-0w after gaining 12.5 points the week before
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next four weeks even after GROCERY_PHARM's weekly improvement decelerates below the 5-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is now within 10 points of its pre-period baseline, indicating high consumer comfort with in-person essential shopping. This restored confidence is expected to spill over quickly into discretionary retail visits within a single week, as the psychological barrier to leaving home for non-essential purposes diminishes alongside essential trips.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is within 10 points of baseline (i.e., greater than -10)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at t-0w stands at -8.4, within 10 points of baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no increase in the week immediately following GROCERY_PHARM crossing within 10 points of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is recovering more slowly than RETAIL_REC and other categories, suggesting outdoor/seasonal leisure activity still lags general reopening. As seasonal conditions and public comfort with outdoor gathering normalize over the coming month, this lag should close, with spillover effects reinforcing sustained growth in retail and recreation visits.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly improvement rate remains less than 50% of RETAIL_REC's weekly improvement rate
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved only 22.3 points over four weeks versus RETAIL_REC's 31.5 point improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth stalls or reverses even as the PARKS-RETAIL_REC improvement gap narrows over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden stall in WORKPLACES recovery after weeks of steady improvement would indicate an abrupt policy or employer-driven halt to office reopening, which would immediately dampen the adjacent foot traffic that has been feeding retail mobility gains, producing a short-term dip in RETAIL_REC within a week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week improvement falls below 5 points after two consecutive weeks of gains above 9 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES gained 9.4, 4.4, and 10.0 points across the last three weeks respectively
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising in the week immediately following a WORKPLACES stall below the 5-point threshold.
